- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 10–30% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 10–25% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp spike in price (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x recent peak or apply decay factor of 0.85.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops sharply after peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply downward bias of 15–25% for 3–7 days post-peak.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing filter or reduce first 3–5 forecast values by 15–20%.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
